lines: Four makers sell phone chargers on this shelf, and you run Ohmly, the violet box. Set your price, then press Next quarter to see who buys.
Ohmly has bought Tidewatt, Sparrow and Kite. Same shoppers, same two years, but now one price covers every box. Press Next quarter.
Both runs, side by side. Tap a rating for each group in Rate the competition.
Your ratings are in. Tap Switch test to see where buyers go after a price rise.
Tap three buyer rows in the comparison table to take their numbers into your memo.
You are the regulator now. Tap a remedy to replay the buyout with it, then weigh its benefits and costs.
Choose one or two reason chips, then pick different first and second remedies.
Pick two evidence chips. Include a ledger difference for your first remedy.
Tap 1. Reasons and choose an opened first remedy. Its ledger will become evidence.
Write your explanation, then tap Check memo. The check looks at structure, not the strength of your argument.
Use the Fix list. Tap Edit explanation, or open 1. Reasons and 2. Evidence to revise your picks.
Tap Save on this device to keep this memo, or revise your explanation. Nothing is sent.
Tap Save on this device to keep this memo, or Edit explanation to revise it. Nothing is sent.
Shoppers are walking to your rivals. Your price or your charger is behind theirs.
Shoppers who leave now have no rival to go to. They keep an old charger instead.
Two years are done. Open Compare to set this run beside the other.
With rivals, a four dollar rise lost half your buyers, most of them to rivals. As the only seller, it lost about one in six, and profit went up.
The buyout goes ahead. Prices climb with every new model.
The deal is blocked. Four sellers keep prices near sixteen dollars.
A year in court, then two sellers. Prices fall, but not to where four sellers kept them.
The cap holds prices down, so the owner builds cheaper chargers to keep its margin.
This cap barely binds, so little changes.
Any maker can now fit the port. Two new makers arrive in the third quarter.
Your memo holds together. Save it, or try another remedy.
Some parts need work. The list shows what to fix.
